use_cases.title: Authenticate to the banking application
use_cases.description: A predefined persona can use the login page to enter username and password, optionally use password visibility and Remember me controls, submit Sign In, and either establish the correct authenticated session for an active credential or receive an understandable failure or locked-state outcome without being granted normal access, with session identity preserved and partially authenticated states avoided.
use_cases.summary: Sign in with a predefined banking persona
use_cases.value: Establishes the correct authenticated boundary and persona-specific banking experience without granting unauthorized access.

cite.quote:
A valid active credential establishes an authenticated session and exposes the
appropriate post-login experience.

cites.quote:
A valid active credential establishes an authenticated session and exposes the
appropriate post-login experience.

Invalid credentials do not grant access and produce an understandable failure state.
AUTH-11 Locked authentication A locked account must not be treated as a normal active session.
An authenticated session must have a clear distinction from the unauthenticated login state.
The application must preserve the appropriate user identity while the session is active.
Session persistence behavior must respect the Remember me control when the feature is implemented.

Expired or invalid sessions must be handled gracefully rather than leaving the user in a partially authenticated
state.

criteria.text: login page presents username, password, password visibility, Remember me, Sign In, and Forgot password controls

cite.quote:
Username/password fields, password visibility control, Remember me, Sign In and Forgot password are
clearly presented.

criteria.text: seven predefined credential fixtures are exposed: standard_user, locked_user, frozen_user, overdraft_user, slow_user, error_user, and admin_user

cite.quote:
standard_user bank_sauce Full access
locked_user bank_sauce Locked account
frozen_user bank_sauce Frozen — no transfers
overdraft_user bank_sauce Negative balance
slow_user bank_sauce Slow loading
error_user bank_sauce Wrong loan total
admin_user admin_sauce Admin view

criteria.text: each credential fixture produces the product state represented by its description

cite.quote: PRD-AC-03 Each credential fixture produces the product state represented by its description.

use_cases.title: End an authenticated session
use_cases.description: An authenticated user can log out so that the active session is terminated, protected banking content stops being actionable as authenticated content, and the product returns cleanly to a non-authenticated state rather than leaving residual access behind.
use_cases.value: Protects banking data and operations by cleanly ending authenticated access.

cite.quote: Logout must terminate the active authenticated session.

cites.quote: Logout must terminate the active authenticated session.
After logout, protected banking content must not remain actionable as an authenticated experience.

Logged out Session terminated Protected banking state is no longer actionable as authenticated
content.
Logout must invalidate the active authenticated experience.

criteria.text: logout terminates the session and makes protected banking content non-actionable as authenticated content

cite.quote: PRD-AC-15 Logout terminates the authenticated experience.

use_cases.title: Access the administrative banking view
use_cases.description: An admin_user can authenticate into the administrative experience, see administrative information and controls that are distinct from ordinary customer-facing banking information, and exercise only those capabilities authorized for the administrative persona while standard users remain excluded from admin-only access.
use_cases.value: Exposes role-specific administrative data and controls only to authorized administrators.

cite.quote: The admin_user fixture represents the administrative view.

cites.quote: The admin_user fixture represents the administrative view.
Administrative authentication must lead to the intended administrative experience.

Administrative information and controls should be distinguishable from ordinary customer-facing banking
information.

Administrative capabilities must be restricted to the administrative persona where the product defines
role-based access.
A standard user must not automatically inherit administrative-only capabilities.
Admin user Receives the administrative view and associated authorized capabilities.

use_cases.title: Transfer money between accounts
use_cases.description: An authenticated user can perform a supported transfer when the current user and account state permits it by selecting a source account, selecting a destination account, entering a monetary amount that passes product validation and sufficient-funds or overdraft rules, and completing the transfer so that frozen users are blocked, failed attempts do not leave partial updates, successful transfers update both balances consistently, and exposed transaction history reflects the committed movement.
use_cases.value: Moves funds while preserving account, permission, and transaction integrity.

cite.quote:
The product provides a supported transfer mechanism where permitted for the current
user/account state.
TRF-02 Source selection A transfer identifies the account from which funds are moved.
TRF-03 Destination selection A transfer identifies the account receiving funds.
TRF-04 Amount A transfer contains a monetary amount subject to product validation.

cites.quote:
The product provides a supported transfer mechanism where permitted for the current
user/account state.
TRF-02 Source selection A transfer identifies the account from which funds are moved.
TRF-03 Destination selection A transfer identifies the account receiving funds.
TRF-04 Amount A transfer contains a monetary amount subject to product validation.

The product must apply its supported balance/overdraft rules when determining whether
a transfer can complete.
TRF-07 Frozen restriction The frozen persona must not be permitted to perform transfers, consistent with its explicit
fixture description.

TRF-08 Atomicity A failed transfer must not leave the source and destination in an inconsistent
partially-updated state.
TRF-09 Balance update A completed transfer must produce consistent source and destination balance changes.
TRF-10 Transaction record A completed transfer must be represented in transaction/activity history where that
feature is exposed.

use_cases.title: Add funds to an account
use_cases.description: Where the live Bank Demo exposes deposit, add-funds, or equivalent balance-increase functionality, an authenticated user can initiate that funding action with a monetary amount that obeys the product's numeric and business rules, commit the increase to the correct balance, have the result reflected in transaction history where supported, and avoid false balances or completed transactions when the operation fails.
use_cases.value: Supports balance increases without corrupting account or transaction state.

cite.quote:
Where the live Bank Demo exposes deposit, add-funds or equivalent balance-increase functionality, it forms part
of the account state-management domain.

cites.quote:
Where the live Bank Demo exposes deposit, add-funds or equivalent balance-increase functionality, it forms part
of the account state-management domain.

Supported users can initiate the product's supported balance-increase operation.
FUND-02 Amount validation The monetary input must obey the application's accepted numeric and business rules.
FUND-03 Balance update A successful funding operation increases the appropriate balance by the committed
amount.
FUND-04 Transaction linkage A successful funding operation is reflected in transaction history where supported.
FUND-05 Failure integrity A failed funding operation must not create a false balance or completed transaction.

use_cases.title: View a role-appropriate banking dashboard
use_cases.description: After a successful active-user login, an authenticated user reaches the banking overview that reflects the current persona, presents or links to relevant accounts, balances, and transaction/activity information, stays consistent with underlying committed state, and differentiates ordinary versus administrative experiences while still rendering the intended persona-specific behavior for exceptional states the product exposes.
use_cases.value: Gives users a consistent overview of their banking state and available banking areas.

cite.quote:
The dashboard is the authenticated banking overview. It should present the user's relevant banking state and
provide access to the application's supported account and transaction capabilities.

cites.quote:
The dashboard is the authenticated banking overview. It should present the user's relevant banking state and
provide access to the application's supported account and transaction capabilities.

A successful active-user login leads to the appropriate authenticated banking experience.
DASH-02 User context The dashboard reflects the authenticated user's persona and associated state.
DASH-03 Account visibility Relevant accounts and balances are represented in the dashboard or reachable through
the banking navigation.
DASH-04 Transaction visibility Relevant transaction/activity information is represented or accessible where supported.
DASH-05 State consistency Dashboard values must remain consistent with the underlying account/transaction state
shown elsewhere in the application.
DASH-06 Role awareness Administrative users receive the intended administrative view rather than being treated
identically to a standard user.

DASH-07 Exceptional states Locked, frozen, overdraft, slow-loading and error-oriented personas must produce their
intended state-specific experience.

use_cases.title: Manage banking accounts
use_cases.description: An authenticated user can view the accounts available to the current user, distinguish each account by displayed identity and type information, see balances and special account states consistently across product surfaces, and, where the live product supports creation, provide required account information, pass validation, create an account, and have it remain available according to the application's persistence model.
use_cases.value: Lets users inspect and, where supported, create accounts while keeping account data accurate and consistent.

cite.quote:
Account management is a core product domain. The product should allow the authenticated user to interact with
supported banking accounts and maintain accurate account-level state.

cites.quote:
Account management is a core product domain. The product should allow the authenticated user to interact with
supported banking accounts and maintain accurate account-level state.

ACCT-01 Account listing The user can view the accounts available to the current user.
ACCT-02 Account identity Each account is distinguishable by its displayed name/identifier and any supported
account type information.
ACCT-03 Account balance Each account exposes a current balance consistent with committed financial operations.
ACCT-04 Account creation Where the live product provides account creation, an authenticated user can provide the
required account information and create an account.
ACCT-05 Account validation Required account fields are validated before an invalid account can be committed.
ACCT-06 Account persistence A successfully created account remains available according to the application's
persistence model.

ACCT-07 Account state Special states such as frozen or overdraft must be reflected accurately in account
behavior and displayed state.
ACCT-08 Account consistency The same account must not display contradictory balances or identity information across
product surfaces.

use_cases.title: Review transaction history
use_cases.description: An authenticated user can view supported transaction or activity information associated with the current banking state, including each transaction's amount, direction, and relevant account association, and rely on the history to represent only committed financial changes, reconcile with displayed balances, persist according to the product model, and avoid misleading completed records when an operation is rejected.
use_cases.value: Makes financial activity observable and reconcilable with account balances.

cite.quote:
Users can view supported transaction/activity information associated with their banking
state.

cites.quote:

TXN-03 Transaction direction Where relevant, the UI distinguishes money entering versus leaving an account.
TXN-04 Transaction account A transaction can be associated with the relevant account(s).
TXN-05 Transaction state Only committed financial changes should be represented as completed financial state.
TXN-06 Balance relationship Completed transactions must reconcile with the displayed account balances.
TXN-07 History persistence Committed transaction history should remain available according to the application's
persistence model.
TXN-08 Failure handling Rejected operations must not create misleading completed transaction records.

use_cases.title: Review loan information
use_cases.description: Where the product exposes loan information, an authenticated or administrative user can view the relevant loan or account context and the current user's loan total, including the intentional wrong-loan-total state for error_user, with the loan view staying internally consistent with supporting data in the same view and without corrupting unrelated balances or transactions.
use_cases.summary: View loan totals and their intentional error state
use_cases.value: Surfaces loan-related totals, including the intentional wrong-loan-total fixture, without corrupting unrelated banking data.

cite.quote:
The existence of the error_user fixture with the description 'Wrong loan total' establishes that the product
includes, or is intended to include, a loan-related total or representation in at least one banking view.

LOAN-04 Consistency Loan totals should be internally consistent with any supporting loan data displayed in the
